interaction.author: agent
interaction.user_prompt: Post-release housekeeping: memo fold, branch sweep, dependabot pass
interaction.model_cot: Three decisions executed. First, the release-manager memo diffed against the full runbook turned out almost entirely redundant - RELEASING.md already contained verification, rollback, and control caveats - so the fold reduced to one genuinely unique piece: the signing-key compromise response, added to Incidents and rollback; the memo file was discarded rather than committed. Second, swept six obsolete branches (five merged remotes plus the superseded pre-DCO branch locally and remotely) on the argument that merged history stays reachable through merge commits, the signed protected tag pins the release point better than any branch, and the pre-DCO variants are unsigned-off commits a DCO-enforcing public repo is better off without. Third, dependabot debt is being merged in severity order (nanoid runtime security bump first, then js-yaml, fast-uri, browserslist, humanfs) honoring the strict up-to-date ruleset serially rather than bypassing it with admin privileges.
